reply.text: Splitting a long run into two shorter efforts is a useful way to build volume when a single long outing feels like too much. Most runners do it as two runs in one day, or a longer run with a short walk break in the middle, which keeps the legs moving without a hard stop. Keep the first chunk easy and conversational, and treat the second as the same easy pace rather than a race against the first. If you tell me your usual long-run distance and how it's been feeling, I can look at your running history and suggest where the split should fall.
